root_cause: checked_add computes `sum = a + b` first and only then tests the result for wrap-around. Signed overflow is undefined behaviour in C, so the overflow has already happened (and an optimising compiler may delete the after-the-fact test). CBMC reports 'arithmetic overflow on signed + in a + b' (checked_add.overflow.1, src/checked_add.c line 10), e.g. with a = INT_MAX and b > 0, and UBSan aborts the positive_overflow / negative_overflow tests with 'signed integer overflow: 2147483647 + 1 cannot be represented in type int'.
rationale: Test the operands, not the result: for b > 0 the sum overflows exactly when a > INT_MAX - b, and for b < 0 exactly when a < INT_MIN - b. Both subtractions are always representable (INT_MAX - b with b > 0, INT_MIN - b with b < 0), so no intermediate overflow is possible, and a + b is only evaluated once it is known to fit. *out is written only on success; the NULL check keeps precedence.
